## cast-as-though-flash

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(op)** an effect op that writes a turn-scoped, per-player timing permission -- "you may cast spells this turn as though they had flash" -- that `legality._timing_ok` consults alongside the printed keyword. It must cover every spell cast for the rest of the turn, including cards not yet in hand when it resolved, and ideally carry an optional selector so narrower printings ("cast creature spells", "cast this spell as though it had flash") reach the same permission
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Casting speed is decided entirely by `legality._timing_ok` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py), which returns True only for `card.is_instant` or `Keyword.FLASH.value in card.keywords` -- printed characteristics read off the CardDef -- and otherwise defers to the sorcery-speed window from `_can_act_at_sorcery_speed`. Nothing writable from an effect widens it. `grant_keyword` with `flash` is the tempting substitute and is wrong twice: `_timing_ok` never reads an object's granted keywords, and even if it did, an `objects` pool resolved at resolution would reach only the cards already in hand, while this line covers the whole turn -- including the card this very spell draws, which is the point of the pairing. `grant_playable` (ops_cards.py) is a *zone* permission (`playable_by`/`playable_turn`), letting a card be cast from somewhere other than hand at its printed timing; it moves no timing restriction. `set_turn_flag` writes a flag only `has_turn_flag` conditions read, and no legality path consults the turn ledger for casting speed. `static_effects` has `cast_from_graveyard` and `cast_from_library_top` -- again zone permissions, not timing ones. The second sentence, "Draw a card.", is plain `draw`, so only the first line is blocked and no partial answer was written. Identical to the block already recorded for Emergence Zone.
- **(op)** an effect op that writes a turn-scoped, per-player timing permission -- "you may cast spells this turn as though they had flash" -- that `legality._timing_ok` consults alongside the printed keyword, ideally with an optional selector so the narrower printings ("cast creature spells", "cast Spirit spells", "cast this spell as though it had flash") and the permanent/static form ("During each opponent's end step, you may cast spells as though they had flash") land on the same permission
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Timing is decided entirely by `legality._timing_ok` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py), which returns True only for `card.is_instant` or `Keyword.FLASH.value in card.keywords` -- printed characteristics read off the CardDef -- and otherwise falls back to the sorcery-speed window from `_can_act_at_sorcery_speed`. Nothing in the game state can widen it. `grant_keyword` with `flash` is the tempting substitute and is wrong twice: `_timing_ok` never reads an object's granted keywords, and even if it did, the grant would reach only the cards sitting in hand when the ability resolved, while the printed line covers every spell cast for the rest of the turn -- cards drawn later, cards cast from other zones, cards that were not yet visible. `grant_playable` (ops_cards.py) is a *zone* permission, not a timing one: it sets `playable_by`/`playable_turn` so a card may be cast from somewhere other than hand, at its printed timing, and it moves no timing restriction at all. `set_turn_flag` writes a flag only `has_turn_flag` conditions read; no legality path consults the turn ledger for casting speed. `become_prepared` and `play_exiled` are both about a specific stashed card, not a standing permission over the whole turn. The rest of the line -- the `{1}` + `tap` + `sacrifice` cost and the mana ability -- is fully expressible; only the effect is missing, so no partial answer was written.

No op mutates the target list of an existing stack object; `counter` is the only other op that touches another spell and it removes it instead of redirecting it. `return_spell_to_hand` likewise takes the spell off the stack.

## divided-damage

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(decision)** a spell-level damage effect that divides a computed total among any number of target creatures as the caster chooses, with the division announced on casting (601.2d) and each target assigned at least 1
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The damage op carries amount/objects/target but no division option, so it would deal the full X to every target; distribute_counters is the only dividing op, it places counters rather than damage, and the notes restrict it to activated abilities with a printed amount
- **(decision)** damage divided as the caster chooses among a variable-size target spec (601.2d): the division is announced while the spell is being cast, at the same time targets are chosen, each chosen target must be assigned at least 1, and the assignments must total the printed amount -- which is what caps 'any number of target creatures' at four here. Concretely a `divided: true` flag on the `damage` op paired with the target spec it consumes, a decision asked during casting that records an amount per chosen ref, and a resolution path in `op_damage` that deals each ref its own recorded share (and deals nothing to a ref that has since become illegal, rather than redistributing).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `op_damage` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/ops_life.py) evaluates one `amount` and deals that full amount to every object in the pool, so `{"op": "damage", "amount": {"const": 4}, "objects": {"target": "t1"}}` over an `"any"`-count spec is 4 damage to *each* target -- unbounded damage from a six-mana instant, not 4 total. The target machinery is not the gap: `TargetSpec.count` already accepts `"any"` (src/commanderblitz/engine/carddef.py) for 'any number of target creatures'. Nothing in `ops`, `value_keys` or `selector_keys` can split one amount across a chosen set: `for_each` iterates a pool but re-runs the same fixed amount per member, `x_value` fixes a single number rather than a vector of them, and no `divide`/`division` concept exists anywhere in src (a grep for it finds only combat damage *assignment order*, 510.1c/banding, which is a different rule and carries no player-chosen split of a spell's damage). Splitting the op into four fixed `damage` ops with four fixed targets would be a different card -- it would forbid 4-to-one and 3/1 and force exactly four legal targets to exist.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

  - Pyrokinesis deals 4 damage divided as you choose among any number of target creatures.
- **Monstrous Onslaught** (rank 13841) — `monstrous_onslaught`

</details>

## set-creature-types

Blocks **2** cards.

- **(static_effect)** a static effect (layer 4) that REPLACES a permanent's creature types with a printed list while it applies -- "is a Dragon ... (It loses all other creature types.)" -- e.g. `subtypes` on the `set_types` static, or a `set_subtypes` static, read in `characteristics` so that, under its `condition`, the permanent's creature subtypes become exactly ["Dragon"] (Human and Noble removed) while its card types and supertypes are untouched. The same shape covers every 'is a <type> ... loses all other creature types' static (Celebration cards, Ixalan-style flip-free shapeshifts).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `set_types` replaces only card types and keeps every subtype whose class is still present (characteristics.py layer 0: `subtypes = {sub for sub in subtypes if SUBTYPE_CLASS.get(sub, 'Creature') in types}`), so `set_types: ["Creature"]` leaves Human Noble in place; `add_subtype` only unions Dragon on top, giving a Human Noble Dragon that a Human or Noble lord would still pump and a Human/Noble filter would still match; the `animate` op's `exact` flag does replace creature types but is a one-shot op with a duration, not a static that switches on and off with the Celebration condition. The rest of the sentence is expressible: the condition is a static `cmp` >= 2 over `{"permanents_entered_this_turn": {"controller": "you", "not_types": ["Land"]}}`, base 4/4 is a `set_pt` static, flying a `grant_keyword` static, and the quoted ability a `grant_ability` static over `grantable_abilities` holding an activated `{R}` pump of Dragons you control -- so only the type replacement is missing, and no partial answer was written.
- **(static_effect)** a static effect (layer 4) that REPLACES a permanent's creature types with a printed list for as long as it applies -- here `affects: {"attached": true}` making the enchanted creature's creature subtypes exactly ["Elk"] (a Human Wizard loses Human and Wizard) -- e.g. `subtypes` on the `set_types` static, or a `set_subtypes` static, read in `characteristics` beside layer 0. The same need as goddric_cloaked_reveler's gap.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `set_types: ["Creature"]` with `affects: {attached: true}` removes the other card types (Artifact) but keeps every subtype whose class is still present (characteristics.py layer 0 keeps creature subtypes because Creature remains), and the loader refuses `set_types` with empty `types`, so the subtypes cannot be wiped and rebuilt with `add_subtype` either; `add_subtype` ["Elk"] only unions, giving a Human Wizard Elk that a Human lord still pumps. The `animate` op's `exact` flag does replace creature types, but it is a one-shot op whose duration is only until_end_of_turn or permanent, so it would outlive the Aura. Everything else is expressible: card-level target `enchanted` (Creature), a self_enters `draw` trigger, and attached statics `lose_all_abilities`, `set_colors` ["G"], `set_types` ["Creature"], `add_subtype` ["Elk"], `set_pt` 3/3 -- so only the creature-type replacement is missing and no partial answer was written.

## activate-only-as-an-instant

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a timing restriction on an activated mana ability that bars it from being activated during the casting or cost-payment of a spell (rule 605.3a / the Lion's Eye Diamond ruling) while leaving it activatable whenever the player has priority: a flag legality and the mana solver both read, so costs.solver_taps and the payment planner never reach for it and only a priority activation can
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: 'sorcery_speed_only' is the opposite restriction -- it narrows activation to the main phase with an empty stack, where this line needs the *wider* instant timing minus the mid-cast window mana abilities uniquely get. 'activation_condition' is documented as a board question ('Activate only if you control five or more Vampires'), checked by legality against the game state, and cannot ask what the player is in the middle of doing. Nothing else in cost_keys or the ability fields describes when an ability may be activated. Dropping the sentence is not neutral: a plain is_mana_ability would be picked up by the solver while paying for another spell, so the engine would discard the player's hand on its own to help pay for a spell -- the precise thing the printed restriction forbids. The near-miss of setting is_mana_ability false hides it from the solver but pays a different price: the mana would then be produced on resolution from the stack, so the ability could be countered or responded to and could not be used to pay for a spell already being cast, which is the only reason anyone plays this card.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Lion's Eye Diamond** (rank 725) — `lion_s_eye_diamond`
  - Discard your hand, Sacrifice this artifact: Add three mana of any one color. Activate only as an instant.

</details>

## basic-land-type-mana

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** Rule 305.6 -- a land with a basic land type has the corresponding intrinsic mana ability ({T}: Add {W}/{U}/{B}/{R}/{G}) by virtue of carrying the subtype, derived in the characteristics pipeline (characteristics.abilities_of) rather than printed on the card, so that a subtype a static ability *grants* brings the mana ability with it. The derived ability must be visible to legality, the payment solver and activation, exactly as the `grant_ability` static already is.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The static effect `add_subtype` says the printed sentence exactly -- {"effect": "add_subtype", "affects": {"types": ["Land"], "controller": "any"}, "subtypes": ["Swamp"]} -- but the engine never derives a mana ability from a subtype. data/cards/basics.cards.json prints "{T}: Add {B}" on Swamp as an ordinary ability, and characteristics.abilities_of returns the printed list plus statics-granted abilities only; nothing consults subtypes. So the static loads clean, every land on the board correctly reads "Land -- Swamp", and not one of them can tap for {B} -- the whole reason the card is played. Urborg itself would also be a land with no mana ability at all, since its {T}: Add {B} is likewise only the 305.6 consequence of being a Swamp. The nearest workaround, a `grant_ability` static handing every land a {T}: Add {B} ability, is not what the card says: it would leave the lands not actually Swamps (invisible to swampwalk, domain, Swamp-fetching searches, and any "nonbasic land" test) while adding an ability the printed line never mentions, and the residual gate would have no printed sentence for it to claim. Dryad of the Ilysian Grove (data/cards/auto/templates.cards.json) already ships with the same construction and the same silent inertness, so closing this fixes both.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth** (rank 73) — `urborg_tomb_of_yawgmoth`
  - Each land is a Swamp in addition to its other land types.

</details>

## cant-be-countered

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** a static ability on a permanent that makes *other* spells uncounterable -- a `cant_be_countered` static whose filter picks the spells it protects (here every spell its controller controls), consulted by the `counter` op against the stack item's controller and characteristics rather than against the casting card's own printed flag, so that a spell cast after this creature is already on the battlefield survives being countered
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The engine's only uncounterable-ness is the card-level `uncounterable` boolean (src/commanderblitz/cards/schema.py -> src/commanderblitz/engine/carddef.py), which the `counter` op reads straight off the spell's own registry definition (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/ops_stack.py) -- it is a printed property of one card, so it can say line 1 ("This spell can't be countered") and nothing more; it cannot be granted, and there is no filter or controller on it. - **(selector)** a player spec (usable as a selector's `controller`, or as `for_each_player.players`) meaning 'each player dealt combat damage by this creature this turn', backed by a per-turn ledger of which players each source object dealt combat damage to
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The selector key `damaged_by` and trigger filter `damaged_by` read `state.damage_ledger`, which records damage to OBJECTS only; the condition `combat_damage_by` is prowl's table-wide 'a player was dealt combat damage by a <subtype>' and names neither the player nor the source object; `select_players` has no spec for damaged players. Emulating it with an unprinted `deals_combat_damage_to_player` trigger that sets a flag would add an ability the card does not print. The rest of the line ({X} cost via `x_value`, `mana_value` X, `not_types: [Land]`, `once_each_turn`) and the {2} pump line are expressible.

  - {X}: Destroy each nonland permanent with mana value X whose controller was dealt combat damage by this creature this turn. Activate only once each turn.

</details>

## power-evasion

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** a block restriction on the attacker that refuses would-be blockers by their DERIVED (current) power at declare-blockers -- "can't be blocked by creatures with power N or less" -- so an anthem, pump spell or +1/+1 counter on the blocker changes whether it may block; e.g. a block_restriction whose blockers filter may carry a derived-power comparison ({"op": "<=", "value": 2}) read from chars in combat.can_block
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: block_restriction's `blockers` filter goes through matches_static, whose `power` key is read at _base_pt (the size before any layer), so a 2/2 given +1/+1 would still be refused and a 3/3 shrunk to 2/2 could still block -- the same reason the engine made skulk a keyword reading derived power instead of a blockers filter. Skulk itself compares against the attacker's power (greater power), not a fixed threshold, so it is a different sentence.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Steel Leaf Champion** (rank 13014) — `steel_leaf_champion`
  - This creature can't be blocked by creatures with power 2 or less.

</details>

## reveal-until-tapped

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a `tapped` option on the reveal_until op, so the card it stops at can be put onto the battlefield tapped (op_reveal_until calls _move_found with tapped=False hard-coded); alternatively an `as` binding on reveal_until naming the found card so a following `tap` op can tap exactly that card
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: reveal_until does the scan, the destination 'battlefield' and the random bottoming exactly, but ignores `tapped`, and the loader refuses `destination_if` (whose branches can carry tapped: true) on anything but search_library/search_zones. reveal_until has no `as`, so a later `tap` cannot name the found land; tapping 'lands you control that entered this turn' would also tap a land played earlier in the turn. Without tapped the card would ramp an untapped land, a strictly better card.

## search-opponent-chooses

Blocks **1** card.

- **(decision)** a `chooser` on `search_library`/`search_zones` (a player spec, so it can be `{"target": ...}`) naming who picks from among the cards the search turned up -- the search itself is still performed and seen by the library's owner, but a *different*, targeted player makes the selection out of the revealed pool. Gifts Ungiven, Intuition and Plea for Power's kin all hang on it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/ops_cards.py) hardcodes the asker: it iterates `select_players(ctx, spec.get("player", "you"))` and passes that same `pid` into `ask_objects(ctx, prompt, pool, 0, take, pid, "search")`, so the searcher is always the chooser. The selector's `chooser` key exists (selectors.py, and it accepts an arbitrary player spec) but a search never routes its selector through `pick_from_pool` -- the selector is only a match test via `_matches_in_zone` -- so writing `chooser` on a search's selector is silently ignored and the caster would pick their own card, which is the entire card. `two_piles` (ops_cards.py) is the only op whose first decision belongs to somebody else, and its splitter is `ctx.opponents()[0]` rather than a target, it reads `library[:amount]` off the top instead of a searched pool, and the *controller* still decides which pile is taken -- the opposite of "target opponent chooses one".

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Intuition** (rank 1971) — `intuition`
  - Target opponent chooses one.
  - Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard.

</details>

## search-split-destinations

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a second destination on `search_library`/`search_zones` for the found-but-not-chosen cards (e.g. `destination: "hand"` plus `rest: "graveyard"`), so one search reveals N, a chosen subset goes one place and the remainder another, with the shuffle still happening once at the end
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` resolves one `DESTINATIONS[spec.get("destination", "hand")]` and hands every picked card to `_move_found` (ops_cards.py); cards that were revealed and not taken simply stay in the library. `look_at_top` is the only lookup with a remainder key, `rest_to_bottom` (ops_cards.py), and it is a boolean hardwired to `_bottom_in_random_order` -- bottom of library, never the graveyard -- besides reading the top N rather than searching. `two_piles` does carry `to`/`other`, but only over the top of the library and only as a pile split. Sequencing two ops instead is an approximation, not the card: `search_library` to the graveyard followed by a `return_from_graveyard` would put all three cards through the graveyard, firing `leaves_graveyard` and inflating `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` from 2 to 3, and `search_library` to hand followed by a `discard` would emit two `discard` events (madness, discard triggers) for cards the printing never discards.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Intuition** (rank 1971) — `intuition`
  - Target opponent chooses one.
  - Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard.

</details>

Dropping the power clause would discount every creature spell.

## spells-cast-per-player

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a value leaf that reports spells cast this turn *per player* rather than summed -- e.g. a `max_spells_cast_of: "each_opponent"`, or a per-player quantifier over a condition -- so "if **an opponent** cast three or more spells this turn" asks whether any single opponent reached three. Wanted by the whole Trap cycle and by storm-watching cards (Mindbreak Trap, Archmage Ascension-style counters, Guttersnipe-adjacent per-seat thresholds).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `alternative_cost` with `{"mana": "{0}"}` and a `condition` is exactly the right home for this line -- that half is not the blocker. The condition itself is: `spells_cast_this_turn` (src/commanderblitz/engine/effects/values.py) resolves its player spec through `select_players` and then **sums** the ledger across every seat it names, so `{"spells_cast_this_turn": "each_opponent"}` is the *total* spells cast by all opponents. At a pod that is a strictly wider card than the printing: three opponents casting one spell each would switch on the free cast, which Mindbreak Trap does not do. The per-player machinery that exists, `max_count_of`/`min_count_of` via `_counts_per_player` (values.py), counts *objects* matching a selector one seat at a time and has no reach into the turn ledger's `spells_cast`; `condition_keys`' `any`/`all` combine sibling conditions and do not quantify over players.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Mindbreak Trap** (rank 539) — `mindbreak_trap`
  - If an opponent cast three or more spells this turn, you may pay {0} rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
  - Exile any number of target spells.

</details>

## static-filter-derived-subtypes

Blocks **1** card.

- **(selector)** a static ability's `affects` filter whose `subtypes` clause matches subtypes granted by layer-4 `add_subtype` statics (here Graaz's own third line, which makes every other creature you control a Juggernaut), so that `attacks_if_able` and `block_restriction` with `affects: {controller: you, subtypes: [Juggernaut]}` reach the creatures the card itself turned into Juggernauts
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: characteristics._matches / _matches_printed read printed subtypes plus obj.added_subtypes (the one-shot add_subtype op) only, never the add_subtype static, so `subtypes: ["Juggernaut"]` on lines 1 and 2 would apply to Graaz alone and skip every creature line 3 makes a Juggernaut -- the whole point of the card. Rewriting the filter as `types: [Creature], controller: you` is a substitution that diverges under text-changing effects on Graaz and type-removing effects with later timestamps, so it is not filed as an answer. Line 3 itself is expressible (set_pt + add_subtype statics with `exclude_self`), and the Wall half of line 2 is `blockers: {subtypes: [Wall]}`

## trigger-filter-any-of

Blocks **1** card.

- **(selector)** an `any_of` disjunction inside a trigger's `filter`, so a `spell_cast` trigger can match a spell that is EITHER noncreature (`not_types: ["Creature"]`) OR has subtype Dragon (`subtypes: ["Dragon"]`), firing once per spell
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: TRIGGER_FILTER_KEYS (engine/triggers.py) has no `any_of`, and validate_trigger_filter refuses it; every listed key is ANDed, so one filter can say only 'noncreature Dragon spell'. `any_types` is an or over card types alone and cannot reach a subtype. Two separate spell_cast triggers (one noncreature, one Dragon) would deal 2 damage for a noncreature Dragon spell (a Kindred Dragon instant or sorcery), which is a different card. The selector and static-filter `any_of` already exists (characteristics._matches_printed, selectors.py), so the trigger-side matcher only needs to recurse the same way
